units.text: Article 114
units.label: Art. 114

units.text: 1. The Government of the Russian Federation:
units.label: Part 1 Art. 114

units.text: а) prepares and submits the federal budget to the State Duma and ensures its execution; submits a report on execution of the federal budget to the State Duma; submits annual reports to the State Duma on the results of its activities, including on questions raised by the State Duma <22>;
units.label: Point «а» Part 1 Art. 114

units.text: б) ensures the implementation of a unified financial, credit and monetary policy in the Russian Federation;
units.label: Point «б» Part 1 Art. 114

units.text: в) ensures the implementation in the Russian Federation of a unified socially oriented state policy in culture, science, education, healthcare, social security, support, strengthening and protection of the family, preservation of traditional family values, and environmental protection;
units.label: Point «в» Part 1 Art. 114

units.text: в.1) ensures state support for the scientific and technological development of the Russian Federation and the preservation and development of its scientific potential;
units.label: Point «в» Part 1 Art. 114 · “в.1) ensures state support for the scientific and technological…”

units.text: в.2) ensures the functioning of a system of social protection for persons with disabilities based on their full and equal exercise of human and civil rights and freedoms, their social inclusion without any discrimination, the creation of an accessible environment for persons with disabilities, and improvement of their quality of life;
units.label: Point «в» Part 1 Art. 114 · “в.2) ensures the functioning of a system of social protection…”

units.text: г) manages federal property;
units.label: Point «г» Part 1 Art. 114

units.text: д) takes measures to ensure national defence and state security and implement the foreign policy of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Point «д» Part 1 Art. 114

units.text: е) takes measures to ensure legality and citizens' rights and freedoms, protect property and public order, and combat crime;
units.label: Point «е» Part 1 Art. 114

units.text: е.1) takes measures to support civil society institutions, including nonprofit organizations, and ensures their participation in developing and implementing state policy;
units.label: Point «е» Part 1 Art. 114 · “е.1) takes measures to support civil society institutions,…”

units.text: е.2) takes measures to support voluntary (volunteer) activity;
units.label: Point «е» Part 1 Art. 114 · “е.2) takes measures to support voluntary (volunteer) activity;”

units.text: е.3) promotes entrepreneurship and private initiative;
units.label: Point «е» Part 1 Art. 114 · “е.3) promotes entrepreneurship and private initiative;”

units.text: е.4) ensures implementation of the principles of social partnership in regulating labour relations and other relations directly connected with them;
units.label: Point «е» Part 1 Art. 114 · “е.4) ensures implementation of the principles of social…”

units.text: е.5) takes measures aimed at creating favourable living conditions for the population, reducing the negative environmental impact of economic and other activities, preserving the country's unique natural and biological diversity, and fostering a responsible attitude towards animals in society;
units.label: Point «е» Part 1 Art. 114 · “е.5) takes measures aimed at creating favourable living…”

units.text: е.6) creates conditions for developing a system of environmental education for citizens and fostering environmental awareness and culture;
units.label: Point «е» Part 1 Art. 114 · “е.6) creates conditions for developing a system of…”

units.text: ж) exercises other powers vested in it by the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal laws and decrees of the President of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Point «ж» Part 1 Art. 114

units.text: 2. The operating procedure of the Government of the Russian Federation is determined by federal constitutional law.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 114

units.text: <22> Point ‘а’ of part 1 is reproduced as amended by the Law of the Russian Federation on an Amendment to the Constitution of the Russian Federation No. 7-ФКЗ of 30 December 2008, ‘On the Supervisory Powers of the State Duma in Relation to the Government of the Russian Federation’, which entered into force on the date of its official publication, 31 December 2008 (Rossiyskaya Gazeta, 2008, 31 December).
units.label: Art. 114 · “<22> Point ‘а’ of part 1 is reproduced as amended by the Law of…”

units.text: Article 115
units.label: Art. 115

units.text: 1. On the basis of and in implementation of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal laws and decrees, executive orders and instructions of the President of the Russian Federation, the Government of the Russian Federation issues resolutions and executive orders and ensures their implementation.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 115

units.text: 2. Resolutions and executive orders of the Government of the Russian Federation are binding in the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 115

units.text: 3. Resolutions and executive orders of the Government of the Russian Federation may be repealed by the President of the Russian Federation if they contradict the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal laws, or decrees and executive orders of the President of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 115

units.text: Article 116
units.label: Art. 116

units.text: The Government of the Russian Federation relinquishes its powers before the newly elected President of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Art. 116 · text

units.text: Article 117
units.label: Art. 117

units.text: 1. The Government of the Russian Federation may tender its resignation, which the President of the Russian Federation accepts or rejects.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 117

units.text: 2. The President of the Russian Federation may decide that the Government of the Russian Federation shall resign.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 117

units.text: 3. The State Duma may express no confidence in the Government of the Russian Federation. A resolution of no confidence is adopted by a majority of the total number of deputies of the State Duma. After the State Duma expresses no confidence, the President of the Russian Federation may announce the Government's resignation or disagree with the State Duma's decision. If the State Duma again expresses no confidence in the Government of the Russian Federation within three months, the President announces the Government's resignation or dissolves the State Duma and calls new elections.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 117

units.text: 4. The Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation may put the question of confidence in the Government to the State Duma, which must consider it within seven days. If the State Duma refuses confidence, the President of the Russian Federation may, within seven days, decide on the Government's resignation or on dissolution of the State Duma and the calling of new elections. If the Government of the Russian Federation again puts the question of confidence to the State Duma within three months and the State Duma refuses confidence, the President decides on the Government's resignation or on dissolution of the State Duma and the calling of new elections.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 117

units.text: 4.1. The Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation, a Deputy Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation or a federal minister may tender their resignation, which the President of the Russian Federation accepts or rejects.
units.label: Part 4.1 Art. 117

units.text: 5. In the event of resignation or relinquishment of powers, the Government of the Russian Federation continues to act on the instructions of the President of the Russian Federation until a new Government is formed. If the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation, a Deputy Chairman or a federal minister is removed from office by the President or resigns, the President may instruct that person to continue performing the duties of the office or assign those duties to another person until the corresponding appointment is made.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 117

units.text: 6. The State Duma may not express no confidence in the Government of the Russian Federation, and the Chairman of the Government may not put the question of confidence in the Government to the State Duma, in the cases provided for by parts 3–5 of Article 109 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, or within one year after the Chairman of the Government is appointed in accordance with part 4 of Article 111 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 117

units.text: Article 118
units.label: Art. 118

units.text: 1. Justice in the Russian Federation is administered only by courts.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 118

units.text: 2. Judicial power is exercised through constitutional, civil, commercial (arbitrazh), administrative and criminal proceedings.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 118

units.text: 3. The judicial system of the Russian Federation is established by the Constitution of the Russian Federation and federal constitutional law. It consists of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation, the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation, federal courts of general jurisdiction, commercial (arbitrazh) courts and justices of the peace of constituent entities of the Russian Federation. Extraordinary courts may not be established.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 118

units.text: Article 119
units.label: Art. 119

units.text: Judges may be citizens of the Russian Federation who have reached 25 years of age, have a higher legal education and at least five years' experience in the legal profession, permanently reside in the Russian Federation and hold neither foreign citizenship nor a residence permit or other document confirming a citizen of the Russian Federation's right to permanent residence in a foreign State. In the manner established by federal law, judges of courts of the Russian Federation are prohibited from opening or holding accounts (deposits) or keeping cash and valuables in foreign banks located outside the territory of the Russian Federation. Federal law may establish additional requirements for judges of courts of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Art. 119 · text

units.text: Article 120
units.label: Art. 120

units.text: 1. Judges are independent and are subject only to the Constitution of the Russian Federation and federal law.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 120

units.text: 2. A court that finds, when considering a case, that an act of a state or other body does not conform to law makes its decision in accordance with the law.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 120

units.text: Article 121
units.label: Art. 121

units.text: 1. Judges have security of tenure.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 121

units.text: 2. A judge's powers may be terminated or suspended only in the manner and on the grounds established by federal law.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 121

units.text: Article 122
units.label: Art. 122

units.text: 1. Judges enjoy immunity.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 122

units.text: 2. A judge may be held criminally liable only in the manner determined by federal law.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 122

units.text: Article 123
units.label: Art. 123

units.text: 1. Proceedings in all courts are open. A closed hearing is permitted in cases provided for by federal law.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 123

units.text: 2. Criminal trials in absentia are not permitted except in cases provided for by federal law.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 123

units.text: 3. Judicial proceedings are conducted on the basis of adversarial procedure and equality of the parties.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 123

units.text: 4. Judicial proceedings are conducted with the participation of jurors in cases provided for by federal law.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 123

units.text: Article 124
units.label: Art. 124

units.text: Courts are funded solely from the federal budget, and funding must ensure the possibility of full and independent administration of justice in accordance with federal law.
units.label: Art. 124 · text

units.text: Article 125
units.label: Art. 125

units.text: 1. The Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation is the highest judicial body of constitutional review in the Russian Federation, exercising judicial power through constitutional proceedings to protect the foundations of the constitutional order and fundamental human and civil rights and freedoms, and to ensure the supremacy and direct effect of the Constitution of the Russian Federation throughout its territory. The Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation consists of 11 judges, including its Chairman and Deputy Chairman.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 125

units.text: 2. At the request of the President of the Russian Federation, the Federation Council, the State Duma, one-fifth of the senators of the Russian Federation or deputies of the State Duma, the Government of the Russian Federation, the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation, or legislative and executive bodies of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation decides cases concerning the conformity with the Constitution of the Russian Federation of:
units.label: Part 2 Art. 125

units.text: а) federal constitutional laws, federal laws, and normative acts of the President of the Russian Federation, the Federation Council, the State Duma and the Government of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Point «а» Part 2 Art. 125

units.text: б) constitutions of republics, charters, and laws and other normative acts of constituent entities of the Russian Federation issued on matters within the jurisdiction of bodies of state authority of the Russian Federation or the joint jurisdiction of bodies of state authority of the Russian Federation and bodies of state authority of its constituent entities;
units.label: Point «б» Part 2 Art. 125

units.text: в) treaties between bodies of state authority of the Russian Federation and bodies of state authority of its constituent entities, and treaties between bodies of state authority of constituent entities of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Point «в» Part 2 Art. 125
